title: Short-edge characterization of exact-marginal discrepancy rounding
status: Full argument derived; internally checked; not independently reviewed or formally verified; priority unestablished
main_statement: For every 0/1 polytope P, k(P)/2 <= b(P) <= 54*k(P), where k(P) is maximum edge Hamming length and b(P) is its universal Euclidean-column-normalized exact-marginal discrepancy radius.
matroid_corollary: For arbitrary matroid base polytopes, exact-marginal rounding with almost-sure l_infinity discrepancy at most 108 for matrices with Euclidean column norms at most one.
sparse_corollary: At most t nonzeros per column, entries bounded by w: matroid basis discrepancy at most 108*w*sqrt(t), with exact marginals; a cost-nonincreasing good basis exists for every prescribed linear objective.
novelty_claim_boundary: Proposed transfer and geometric characterization, not invention of the existing retained-row spectral potential, deletion accounting, or normalized resolvent method.
proof_ingredients: vanishing linear tilt and finite-set separation
assumptions: each column has Euclidean norm at most one
not_claimed: constant bounds for arbitrary matroid intersections
constructive_proof_gate: Replace compact nonconvex minimization with a polynomial-bit face-preserving procedure, charging barrier precision, changing faces, coefficient truncation, rational state restoration, and global progress.
